newsitem.title: USA: Lott "greatly depressed" by Clinton budget.
newsitem.headline: Lott "greatly depressed" by Clinton budget.

text.p: Senate Republican Leader Trent Lott said Friday he was "greatly depressed" and disappointed by President Clinton's fiscal 1998 budget plan.
Lott told a news conference he reached the conclusion after studying the budget, presented Thursday, for an additional 24 hours.
"I must tell you I am greatly depressed by what I've seen," Lott said. "I had hoped for more leadership and a greater degree of courage in making recommendations to the Congress."
He said he had called Clinton and expressed his concerns.
"This is a disappointment," Lott said. "So much of this budget is recooked from last year."
He said the budget contained "optimistic assumptions, shellgames and triggers" and also added entitlement spending -- "what looks like at least $60 billion."
